t: Crime Scene Solvers: Céline Marchand Case
d: On May 30th 2015 in Sorinières, Yann Machand reports his wife Céline Marchand missing.

t: Crime Scene Solvers: Murderous Lovers - Anne Bardot
d: The disturbing missing case in Paris of 4 years old.

t: Crime Scene Solvers: Killer Cop (Tavernier Case)
d: Firefighters in Barbizieux, Charente, are called to a fire in a large house in the village. They arrive to find the lifeless body of the owner, Claude Tavernier, 83, lying in a large pool of blood.

t: Copycat Killers
d: Vincent Ellerbe and James Irons recreate a deadly heist, inspired by Money Train.

t: Copycat Killers
d: Ari Squire fakes his death after watching Forensic Files, aiming to collect life insurance.

t: Copycat Killers
d: James Cushing imitates Lizzie Borden’s ax murder after watching The Legend of Lizzie Borden.

t: Copycat Killers
d: Jason Moore recreates Freddy Krueger's weapon to kill his only friend, inspired by A Nightmare on Elm Street.

t: Dr. G: Medical Examiner: Body Burn
d: A bipolar man's family fears he took his own life and turn to Dr. G for closure. At autopsy, Dr. G makes a shocking discovery that threatens to turn the whole case upside down.

t: Dr. G: Medical Examiner: Truth of the Matter
d: Carol Moleskie agrees to go on a hunting excursion with her husband, Bob. A few hours after they enter the woods, they emerge again, Bob frantically waving down traffic as he carries his bloody wife.

t: Dr. G: Medical Examiner: Shock to The System
d: Police discover the dead body of Andrew Hopper clutching a syringe and covered with blood. The body is in Dr. G’s hands, as are the clues to solving the case.

t: Dr. G: Medical Examiner: Deadly Journey
d: Dr. G reviews a woman's medical records and learns that she suffered from an auto-immune disease called lupus, which might have something to do with her death.

t: Dr. G: Medical Examiner: Deadly Business
d: Dr. G. has just graduated from medical school and is set to begin her first job as an M.E. in Jacksonville, Florida when a high-profile case challenges her to use her newly acquired skills.

t: Conmen Case Files: Robert Hendy-Freegard – The Terrorist Trickster
d: Dubbed “The Most Evil Conman Ever” by the British press, Hendy-Freegard terrorized victims into believing they were terrorist targets.

t: Conmen Case Files: Gene Morrison – Fraudulent Forensics Expert
d: He faked his own credentials and netted $400,000 of taxpayers money, giving bogus court testimony and investigative services.

t: Conmen Case Files: Carl Hildebrandt – The Dead Con Artist
st: Carl Hildebrandt – The Dead Con Artist
d: Hildebrandt faked his own death and stole the identity of a dead child to escape criminal charges before fleeing to Florida.

t: 72 Hours: The Ghost
d: A cunning arsonist stays one step ahead of the police and terrifies a small farming community until behavioural profiling help detectives zero in on a very unlikely suspect.

t: 72 Hours: Nightmare
d: Every woman’s worst nightmare comes to life when a bearded sexual predator starts attacking women in the safety of their own apartments while they are sleeping.

t: 72 Hours: Fat Bandit
d: A string of bank robberies in Winnipeg confound local police. Most bank-robbers are addicts, usually quite thin. This new man doesn't fit the profile: this bandit is fat.

t: 72 Hours: Sweet Killer
d: An aging hippy is going through bad times. When he's found dead in his home with a gut of antifreeze, it's a closed case. Then a shocking confession reveals a maelstrom of lies and a story of cold-blooded murder.

t: 72 Hours: Monster of Miramichi
d: Firemen are called to a blaze and discover two sisters, one dead and the other on death's door. Detectives learn that a man snuck in and brutally sexually assaulted the sisters before setting fire to the house.

t: 72 Hours: Double Cross
d: The investigation of the murder of a shady Montreal businessman takes detectives into the lurid underworld of drug dealers, con men, and crooked lawyers.
